p: tore his clothes: In sign of grief and repentance.

Isaiah the prophet the son of: To have comfort from him by the word of God, that his faith might be confirmed and so his prayer be more earnest: teaching by it that in all dangers these two are the only remedies to seek to God and his ministers.
birth: We are in as great sorrow as a woman in labour who cannot be delivered.
hear the words of Rabshakeh: That is, will declare by effect that he has heard it: for when God defers to punish, it seems to the flesh, that he knows not the sin, or hears not the cause.
lift up thy prayer for the: Declaring that the ministers office stands not only in comforting by the word, but also in praying for the people.
rumour: Of the Egyptians and Ethiopians, who will come and fight against him.
Libnah: Which was a city toward Egypt, thinking by it to have stayed the force of his enemies.

deceive thee: Thus God would have him utter a most horrible blasphemy before his destruction: as to call the author of all truth a deceiver: some gather by this that Shebna had disclosed to Sennacherib the answer that Isaiah sent to the king.
Gozan: Which was a city of the Medes.
Haran: Called also Charre a city in Mesopotamia, from which Abraham came after his fathers death.
dwellest between the cherubim: He grounds his prayer on God's promise, who promised to hear them from between the Cherubims.
their countries: Meaning, the ten tribes.
all the kingdoms of the earth: He declares for what cause he prayed, that they might be glorified by it through all the world.
virgin: Whom God had chosen to himself as a chaste virgin, and over whom he had care to preserve her from the lusts of the tyrant, as a father would have over his daughter.
Holy One of Israel: Declaring by this that they who are enemies to God's Church fight against him whose quarrel his Church only maintains.

and drank water: He boasts of his policy in that he can find means to nourish his army: and of his power in that his army is so great, that it is able to dry up whole rivers, and to destroy the waters which the Jews had closed in.

that I have formed it: Signifying that God did not make his Church to destroy it, but to preserve it: and therefore he says that he formed it of old, even in his eternal counsel which cannot be changed.
before it is grown up: He shows that the state and power of most flourishing cities endures but a moment in respect to the Church, which will remain forever, because God is the maintainer of it.
going out: Meaning, his counsels and enterprises.
hook in thy nose: Because Sennacherib showed himself as a devouring fish and furious beast, he uses these similarities to teach how he will take him and guide him.
camest: You will lose your labour.

sign to thee: God gives signs after two sorts: some go before the thing as the signs that Moses worked in Egypt, which were for the confirmation of their faith, and some go after the thing, as the sacrifice, which they were commanded to make three days after their departure: and these latter are to keep the blessings of God in our remembrance, of which sort this here is.
He promises that for two years the ground would feed them of itself.
the remnant that hath escaped of: They whom God has delivered out of the hands of the Assyrians will prosper: and this properly belongs to the Church.
David's sake: For my promise sake made to David.
Nineveh: Which was the chiefest city of the Assyrians.
Esarhaddon his son reigned in his: Who was also called Sardanapalus, in whose days ten years after Sennacherib's death the Chaldeans overcame the Assyrians by Merodach their king.
